primary_issue: The shatter event is not readable or forceful (no clear central hole/“explosion outward”, very few visible shards), and the shot composition/lighting makes the key action get lost in the frame.
issues: Shatter lacks impact: no convincing outward burst of shards; fracture pattern is faint/sparse and doesn’t communicate a high-speed brick strike.
Brick is not clearly readable as a heavy red clay brick flying in from frame-left at speed; the “through the window trailing fragments” story is not visible.
Requested gritty derelict industrial warehouse look is not achieved: materials/props read as clean, simple primitives (blockout/placeholder feel).
Window is too small in frame / action occupies too little screen space; large empty wall areas dominate, reducing drama and clarity.
Lighting doesn’t sell cinematic night mood: scene feels flat, with insufficient specular/rim lighting on glass to make shards pop; dark interior swallows detail.
Rusted steel frame + aged concrete wall are not convincingly represented (frame reads more like clean trim/wood; wall lacks concrete wear/grime).
No motion cues (e.g., motion blur/streaking) to sell high-speed impact in this still frame; little sense of energy or debris trail.
suggestions: Recompose so the window/impact fills much more of the frame (closer camera or tighter crop); make the impact point the visual center of attention.
Increase fracture/shard detail and readability (denser micro-fractures + more breakup): try raising Voronoi density (Line 148: voronoi Scale 24.0 → ~35–50).
Increase high-frequency crack detail: Line 370 noise Scale 9.0 → ~15–25; Line 371 noise Detail 7.0 → ~9–12; Line 206 noise Roughness 0.7 → ~0.8–0.9.
Make cracks/shards catch light more strongly via normal/bump shaping: Line 372 bump Strength 0.1 → ~0.2–0.35; Line 373 bump Distance 0.02 → ~0.005–0.01 (sharper micro-relief).

If the shader uses wave/noise to form crack striations, push toward finer, more chaotic breakup: Line 368 wave Scale 14.0 → ~20–35; Line 369 wave Distortion 1.2 → ~1.8–2.5; Line 310 wave Detail Scale 2.0 → ~4–8.
Lift ambient just enough so the glass event doesn’t disappear into black: Line 92 world Strength 0.08 → ~0.15–0.30 (keep it moody, but readable).
If emission is being used to make cracks visible, increase it carefully (Line 410 emission Strength): try ~2×–4× for the crack component only (avoid making the whole pane glow unnaturally).

Art direction fixes (not just params): add believable rusted steel + aged concrete textures (roughness variation, grime, edge wear), and more warehouse set dressing/atmosphere so it reads ‘derelict industrial at night’.

Physics/story clarity: ensure the sim produces a clear blown-out impact hole, lots of varied shard sizes, and a visible debris trail behind the brick; add motion blur for the brick and fastest shards to sell speed.
vision_assessment: The image shows a simple warehouse-like interior with a large flat wall and a small window on the right, lit by a warm wall-mounted light. The environment and props (boxes/barrel) look like basic primitives with minimal texture/weathering, so it does not read as a gritty derelict industrial warehouse. The glass impact itself is hard to see: there’s only a faint/sparse cracking/shatter near the window and very little visible shard ejection. The brick is not clearly identifiable as a heavy red clay brick traveling fast from the left, and the overall composition leaves the key event too small and visually subdued.
